# Audit: #779 3-arm ablation CPU phases (scaling grid + fits) — vectorization/optimization

Audited (read-only): `.claude/worktrees/issue-779/scripts/issue779_scaling_grid.py` (CLI),
`.claude/worktrees/issue-779/src/explore_persona_space/experiments/issue_779/{scaling_grid,fit_h,metrics}.py`,
plan `tasks/followups_running/779/plans/v6.md` §9, worktree `orchestrate/env.py`.
Benchmarked on this VM at 8 threads: f64 GEMM ~165 GFLOPS, f64 SVD (gesdd) ~11 GFLOPS effective.

## 1. Cell count + wall-time

- Grid: 7×7 − 1 = 48 cells × K=10 subsamples = 480 (h + g) ridge fits per `run_scaling_grid`
  call; 18 calls (3 traits × 2 modes × 3 variants: natural / 1:1-upsample / secondary-10rollout)
  = **8,640 grid cells ≈ 17,280 ridge fits, each with its own (N×3584) float64 SVD** (N up to
  ~7,000; nL axis max 5000, nB max ~2,000-2,400 realized).
- Arm comparison: 3 traits × 2 modes × 2 aggs × 4 arms = 48 full-N fits (N = 2.4k–9.8k) + 48
  pv_pinv compact SVDs (the P/Q O(H·r²) path — good, but r = 3584 = H for full arms so it is
  effectively dense there).
- Layer matrix: 3 traits × 28 layers × 2 full-arm fits = 168 fits + 100 label-shuffle nulls × 2
  readouts per layer (cheap, n_boot=1).
- Bootstrap: ~8,640 cells × 2 DVs × 2 modes × 1000 replicates ≈ 3.5e7 replicate evaluations
  ≈ 2.2e8 per-condition `np.corrcoef` calls in pure-python loops.

FLOP accounting (per 5000-row h fit): SVD 2.6e11 + UtY 1.3e11 + **GCV loop 13 × U@(filt·UtY)
GEMMs ≈ 1.7e12** + W=P@Q 0.9e11 ≈ 2.2 TFLOP — ~78% is the GCV Yhat materialization.
Per grid call ≈ 3.1e14 FLOPs ≈ ~50 min at measured throughput → grid ≈ **15 h**, + layer
matrix ~1.5 h (incl. 84 full `torch.load`s of the multi-GB corpus bundle) + arm comparison
~0.5 h + bootstrap ~1 h ⇒ **~18–20 h single-process at 8 capped threads** (longer under fleet
contention or uncapped). Plan v6 §9 sized this at **1.5 wall-h ("ridge closed-form … cheap CPU
reductions")** — the implementation is ~12× over its own plan estimate. **NOT acceptable as-is.**

## 2. Per-item verdicts

- **(a) Ridge fits — GAP (multiple).** Closed-form SVD ridge, no AdamW (good); ONE SVD reused
  across the 13 λ values (good). But:
  (i) the GCV loop materializes `Yhat_tr = U @ (filt[:,None] * UtY)` per λ —
  `experiments/issue_779/scaling_grid.py:294-302` and `fit_h.py:82-90` — 13 needless
  (N,r)@(r,H) GEMMs ≈ 78% of big-fit FLOPs; rss is computable in O(r·H) per λ via
  `rss(λ) = ||Y_c||²_F − Σ_j (2·filt_j − filt_j²)·||UtY[j,:]||²`.
  (ii) `fit_g_cell` → `F.ridge_fit_predict` re-runs a fresh SVD of the SAME X the h fit just
  decomposed (`scaling_grid.py:453` → `fit_h.py:77`) — ~2× on the SVD cost.
  (iii) Full-row cells recompute identical fits K=10×: `_subsample_indices` clamps to n_avail
  (`scaling_grid.py:97-105`), so at nL=5000 (all rows) / nB=corpus-max the 10 "subsamples" are
  permutations of the same set and ridge is permutation-invariant — the most expensive row of
  the grid is 90% redundant.
  (iv) `W = P @ Q` (2·N·H² / 2·H²·r) is formed for EVERY grid cell (`_ridge_fit`,
  `scaling_grid.py:306`) though grid cells consume only dot/cos readouts — pred should be
  `(Xev_n @ P) @ Q` (or `P @ (Q @ r_b)` for the dot), W only needed in `run_arm_comparison`.
  (v) The known-good torch-eigh Gram-space `_ridge_fit_predict_fast` + in-process equivalence
  gate exists IN THIS WORKTREE (`scripts/issue779_percontext_recon.py:83,569-593`) and is not
  reused ("reuse existing in-repo tools" miss). Batching across traits/layers/cells is genuinely
  impossible (each cell has a distinct train matrix) — the per-cell closed form is the right
  primitive; the waste is inside each fit + across duplicate fits.
- **(b) MLP fits — N/A (none).** The implemented grid is ridge-only; no serial AdamW anywhere.
  Note: plan v6 promises a `{ridge, mlp}` 2-method grid (+ ~1 GPU-h A100 MLP arm) and
  `fit_h.mlp_fit_predict` exists but is never called by the grid CLI — a planned-vs-actual
  coverage note for the analyzer, not a perf gap.
- **(c) Grid size/wall-time — FLAG.** See §1: ~18–20 h vs plan's 1.5 h and the audit's ~1-2 h bar.
- **(d) Bootstrap CIs — GAP.** `metrics.py:81-87` loops 1000 replicates × conditions ×
  `np.corrcoef`. The bootstrap resamples CONDITIONS only, and per-condition r + the
  std/min_n exclusion set are replicate-invariant ⇒ precompute the per-condition r vector once;
  each replicate is a gather+mean over an (n_boot, n_cond) index matrix — ~1000× less python,
  removes ~1 h.
- **(e) Memory — PARTIAL.** LMSYS bundle (6.02 GB) `torch.load`ed once, held resident (no mmap);
  per-layer slices converted to f64 on demand (~143 MB each) — fine. But `load_corpus_source`
  re-`torch.load`s the full behavior-corpus bundle (multi-GB v_x) on EVERY call:
  28×3 = 84 times in `run_layer_matrix` (`issue779_scaling_grid.py:253` via `:438`) + 12 in the
  main loop ⇒ ~300+ GB of redundant disk reads. Load once per trait (or `mmap=True`) and slice
  per layer. Peak RSS ~10–15 GB — safe vs earlyoom on the 128 GB VM.
- **(f) Thread caps — GAP.** The worktree predates the #847 merge: its
  `src/explore_persona_space/orchestrate/env.py` has NO OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS setdefault (grep: zero
  hits), the grid CLI sets no `torch.set_num_threads`, and the worktree's `issue779_layer_sweep.py`
  also lacks the cap present on main (:486). Launched from the worktree as-is ⇒ uncapped BLAS on
  the shared VM — the exact load-226 regression. Fix: rebase the worktree onto main (its
  `load_dotenv()` call at CLI line 52 then inherits the setdefault) or launch with inline
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 MKL_NUM_THREADS=8 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=8 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=8`.
- **(g) Checkpointing — PARTIAL.** `write_json_atomic` whole-dict rewrites per (trait, mode) for
  arm_comparison/scaling_grid/g_holdout (CLI :744-746) + per trait for the layer matrix (:764) —
  crash-safe files, but NO load-partial-and-skip on restart: a crash loses up to a full
  (trait, mode) block (~1–3 h at current speed) and a re-run recomputes from zero.
- **(h) Routing — PARTIAL.** Plan §9: grid/ridge off-pod on VM CPU ("cheap"), MLP arm → 1×A100
  (unimplemented), corpus pod released before the CPU phase — no GPU pod held (no #778 pattern),
  footprint ~7–15 GB < 50 GB VM cap (OK). But an ~18–20 h CPU phase on the shared VM violates the

## Mentor ask
Compare projecting prompt-side context states onto `w_pinv = pinv(M) @ r_B` (the
min-norm preimage — the prompt-space vector that maps TO the persona vector under
the fitted context->answer map M) against the `w = r_B` baseline (pv_raw) and the
transpose read `w = M^T r_B` (== the stage-1 linear-h dot read `r1_ridge_dot`).

## Method (reused stage-1 rig verbatim)
- M = the LINEAR ridge map c_x -> v(x) refit at each trait's frozen read-out layer
  (evil L14 / sycophancy L26 / hallucination L17), stage-1 recipe: standardize-X,
  center-Y, GCV lambda over logspace(-2,4,13), closed-form SVD, n_train = all 5000
  LMSYS contexts (pass_b). **M reproduces stage-1 exactly**: recon R2 = 0.8327 /
  0.8340 / 0.8602 matches committed stage1_headline.json (0.832659 / 0.834045 /
  0.860174) to 4 dp; the W-vs-library prediction path agreed to max|Δpred|=0.00e+00.
- M convention: stage-1 predicts v = c_std @ W + ymu, so for v = M c_std, M = W^T.
  Then w_tr = M^T r_B = W r_B; w_pinv = pinv(M) r_B = pinv(W^T) r_B (both read on
  STANDARDIZED eval c, the fitted-map frame == r1_ridge_dot). pv_raw = raw c . r_B,
  verbatim stage-1.
- pinv via truncated SVD of M. Pre-registered headline rank = ridge-estimable rank
  #{i: s_i(X_std)^2 >= lambda} (TRAIN-only, frozen before the eval read; k* = 1433 /
  1321 / 1565). Full-rank pinv + a rank sweep {5..full} reported as diagnostics.
- Eval read: within-condition Pearson r vs the graded judge trait score (PV
  convention; bootstrap CI resamples conditions), on the persona-vectors eval grid
  (8 system + 5 many-shot conditions x 20 questions), pass_a.
- ORIENTATION SANITY (transposed-orientation blocker checked independently): M maps
  context->answer, so pinv(M) maps answer->context and w_pinv lives in CONTEXT space.
  M @ w_pinv -> r_B residual = 0.000 at full rank for all 3 traits (exact preimage);
  at the truncated headline rank the residual is the r_B energy outside M's top-k
  left-singular subspace (~0.17-0.30). Orientation CONFIRMED correct.
- Null discipline (#778): norm-matched random-direction null in standardized-c space,
  n=200 draws, per mode.

| trait | mode | pv_raw (r_B) | transpose (M^T r_B) | pinv (M^+ r_B, k*) | null p95|r| |

| evil | system | +0.172 | -0.078 | **+0.289** | 0.297 |
| evil | many-shot | +0.417 | +0.269 | **+0.455** | 0.455 |
| sycophancy | system | **+0.602** | +0.541 | +0.442 | 0.377 |

| hallucination | system | **+0.456** | +0.401 | +0.282 | 0.413 |

(bold = best of the three; bootstrap 95% CIs in the JSON)

## Findings
1. **No consistent win for the pseudoinverse direction.** pinv beats BOTH raw pv and
   transpose for evil (both modes) and hallucination many-shot, but LOSES to both for
   sycophancy (both modes) and hallucination system-prompt. The best direction is
   trait- and mode-dependent — no direction dominates.
2. **This does NOT overturn #779's Takeaway** that the learned map fails to beat the
   raw projection. The pinv adds a third fitted-map-derived direction that also fails
   the consistency bar; the raw persona vector remains the most reliable single monitor
   (best or within-CI-of-best in 3 of 6 cells, never catastrophically bad).
3. **Specificity is weak for ALL methods (the #778 bar).** The norm-matched
   random-direction null p95|r| is large (system 0.30-0.41, many-shot 0.41-0.46)
   because within-condition mean r over few conditions (8 system / 5 many-shot) x ~20
   questions is high-variance and a random 3584-dim direction already reaches |r|~0.4
   by chance. Evil's pinv wins (+0.289 sys, +0.455 many) sit AT/BELOW their null
   p95 — not distinguishable from a random direction. Only sycophancy (all reads
   0.44-0.70) and hallucination-many pinv (+0.551 > 0.444) clear the bar with margin.
   This bounds how strongly ANY of these headline numbers (incl. #779's own pv_raw /
   transpose rows) can be read at this condition count.
4. **Severe rank-truncation contingency (ill-conditioning).** cond(M) = 2.5e5-1.4e6.
   FULL-rank (raw min-norm) pinv collapses — evil many-shot full-rank r = -0.215 —
   because it amplifies M's tiny singular directions (1/sigma). The "good" pinv reads
   live only at intermediate truncation; the frozen ridge-estimable k* is a reasonable
   (not argmax) point. Sweep in the JSON + figure; no oracle rank selection on eval.
5. **Geometry:** w_pinv is nearly orthogonal to r_B (cos ~0.01-0.25 across ranks) — the
   min-norm preimage is NOT just recovering the persona vector. It aligns with the
   transpose only at low rank (cos ~0.6-0.86), diverging as rank grows. The transpose
   itself also rotates far from r_B (cos(M^T r_B, r_B) = 0.088 / 0.201 / 0.062).

| trait | pv_raw group r | map h group r | paired diff h−raw [95% CI] | P(diff>0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Findings
1. **At the matched pre-registered layers, the map's persona-level read beats the
   raw persona-vector projection in all 3 traits, paired 95% CIs excluding zero**

## The ask (verbatim)
> do we have evaluation on generic prompts?

Established first that only hallucination is evaluable on generic prompts:
per-context LMSYS judge labels score >50 on 24.6% of 4593 judged prompts for
hallucination vs 0.2% (evil) / 6.0% (sycophancy) — evil and sycophancy have no
positive class to test against on generic prompts. So this run tests the one
answerable case.

## Method (reuses issue779_arm_headline.py GramRidge + loaders verbatim)
At the frozen read-out layer L17, predict the per-context LMSYS hallucination
judge label from the pre-generation context state (pass_b, cx_last), three reads:
(a) pv_raw <c, r_B> — the original Persona Vectors method, no fit; (b) map read
<h(c), r_B>, h = GramRidge context->answer profile, 5-fold held-out; (c) direct
ridge probe c->label, 5-fold held-out. Metrics: Pearson + Spearman vs the label
(2000-draw bootstrap CIs), AUROC on the >50 binary, and a read-decile mean-label
curve. n = 4593 judged contexts. pass_b staged locally, r_B @ 037fcbb, labels =
lmsys_g_labels.json (be260f08). CPU, ~2 min, 0 GPU-h.

## Headline
| read | Pearson [95% CI] | Spearman | AUROC | decile mean-label bottom->top | top-bottom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pv_raw <c,r_B> | -0.030 [-0.058,-0.000] | -0.016 | 0.479 | 25.9 -> 20.3 | -5.6 |
| map <h(c),r_B> (CV) | -0.008 [-0.036,+0.021] | -0.004 | 0.493 | 22.6 -> 22.5 | -0.1 |
| direct probe c->label (CV) | -0.001 [-0.031,+0.027] | +0.002 | 0.499 | 25.0 -> 24.3 | -0.7 |

## Findings
1. **Clean null: none of the reads predict generic-prompt hallucination.** All
   three AUROCs are ~0.50, all Pearson CIs include/sit at zero, and the decile
   mean-label curves are flat or slightly INVERTED (pv_raw top decile 20.3 <
   bottom 25.9). Ranking generic prompts by any read does not sort them by
   answer hallucination.
2. **The supervised probe is decisive.** probe_g_cv is fit DIRECTLY on the
   labels (5-fold held-out) — the best case for decodable signal — and lands at
   Pearson -0.001 / AUROC 0.499. So this is not a wrong-read-out failure fixable
   by a better direction: there is no linearly decodable generic-prompt
   hallucination signal in the pre-generation state. Reproduces AND generalizes
   #1092's within-LMSYS hallucination floor (cross-validated r 0.009) to the raw
   PV direction and the map read.
3. **The monitoring signal is rig-specific.** On the crafted Persona-Vectors grid
   these same reads score 0.5-0.8 (persona-level averaging reaches 0.53 for
   hallucination); that signal is a property of the constructed trait-eliciting
   system prompts, and does not survive the move to naturalistic one-off prompts.

## Caveat (mechanism ambiguous, conclusion not)
LMSYS labels are 1 rollout x 5 judge draws, mean-only (no per-draw). Much of a
single rollout's hallucination label is generation stochasticity no pre-gen read
could predict in principle; with 1 rollout the generation-noise and
judge-reliability ceilings are not estimable here. Cannot separate "state does
not encode generic hallucination propensity" from "single-rollout label too
noisy to have a decodable target" — both imply you cannot monitor generic-prompt
hallucination from the pre-gen state with these labels. A clean version needs
k>=5 rollouts/prompt (predict the per-prompt hallucination RATE) + a
judge-reliability ceiling.

selected on the outer-train ONLY (fit-free methods by outer-train correlation;
corpus-fit methods by 4-fold inner CV), then evaluated on the held-out outer-test.
Reads z-scored per fold (label-free) before pooling. Report z-pooled Pearson r over
60 + per-fold mean±SD + paired bootstrap vs pv_raw. Six methods x three traits.
Reuses arm_headline GramRidge/loaders; pass_b + corpus local; 0 GPU-h.

## Findings
1. **The deployable generic map does NOT reliably beat raw** — ties evil +
   sycophancy (paired CIs straddle zero), small win hallucination (+0.073, CI
   excludes zero). 1 win / 2 ties. Confirms the recollection that the map does
   not beat the original method on held-out contexts; the correct statement is
   PARITY with a small hallucination edge.
2. **Reconciles the swings:** corpus-LOGO+frozen (my 1st claim, +0.08-0.12) was
   in-distribution+frozen -> too favorable; generic+frozen (my "correction",
   loses halluc -0.19) -> frozen layers L14/L17 bad for the map -> too harsh;
   argmax sweep (wins 21-22/28) -> selection-optimistic; nested CV -> parity.
   All prior swings were layer-selection artifacts.
3. **Deployable direct predictor g_generic is decisively WORST** (loses all 3,
   -0.256/-0.397/-0.575, CIs exclude zero) — the supervised probe does not
   transfer; single most robust result across every analysis.
4. **The oracle ceiling is only +0.05-0.11 above raw** — at persona level the raw
   projection already nearly saturates the answer-reading ceiling, so there is
   almost no headroom for any pre-generation method to beat raw. This is WHY
   nothing beats raw much.
5. **Only g_corpus clearly beats raw** (syco +0.114, halluc +0.219, ~oracle) but
   needs judged behavior labels on the trait corpus. map_corpus ~= map_generic
   ~= raw: the learned map's value proposition does not survive honest CV.
